headline: A Bloomberg analysis finds that gas plants proposed to power data centers could raise US power-sector emissions by about a fifth.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the analysis was published 18 Aug 2026, so it is not new today.
importance_line: Residents near the plants and the climate goals of Amazon and Microsoft are affected, but the 20% figure assumes every proposed plant is built, which Bloomberg says is unlikely.
summary: Bloomberg reports, in an analysis published 18 Aug 2026 and carried by Fortune, that 99 proposed on-site gas power plants for data centers tracked by BloombergNEF would emit about 318 million metric tons of carbon dioxide a year, enough to lift US power-sector emissions by about 20% and by as much as a third if run flat out. Bloomberg notes that not every proposed plant is likely to be built.
notes: Older news re-dated by EnergyNow on 4 Oct 2026. Credited to Bloomberg (first reporter); text read at Fortune.
